questions.question:

Volume of a cylinder = πr²h

⇒ 6006 = (22 × 49 × 13)⁄7 × x³

⇒ 6006 = 2002x³

⇒ x³ = 6006 ÷ 2002 = 3

⇒ x = ∛3

Now, radius = 7x = 7 × ∛3 = 7 × 3(1)/(3) cm

**∴ The correct answer is **7 × 3(1)/(3)** cm.**

**Solution:**

questions.question: What is the total surface area of a cylinder having radius of base as 4.2 cm and height as 8 cm?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the base (r) = 4.2 cm.

Height (h) = 8 cm.

**Formula Used:**

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a cylinder = 2πr(r + h)

**Calculation:**

First, calculate the sum of radius and height:

r + h = 4.2 + 8

r + h = 12.2 cm

Now, calculate the Total Surface Area:

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2 × π × r × (r + h)

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2 × (22/7) × 4.2 × 12.2

⇒ TSA = 2 × (22/7) × 4.2 × 12.2

⇒ TSA = 322.08 cm²

**The total surface area of the cylinder is 322.08 cm².**

questions.question: Find the total surface area of a cylinder whose radius is 7 cm and curved surface area is 3520 cm² (use π = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Total Surface Area** (TSA) = **Curved Surface Area** (CSA) + 2 × **Base Area**

Base Area = πr² = (22/7) × 7 × 7 = 154 cm²

TSA = 3520 + 2 × 154 = 3520 + 308 = 3828 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 3828 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Radius** (r) of the cylinder = 7 cm

**Curved Surface Area** (CSA) = 3520 cm²

**Formula Used:**

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2πrh + 2πr²

Where, 2πrh = Curved Surface Area (CSA)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d7415fe53083990c16b901238a82a14fec30b11ba8cb2853c1a4ade3a21709c1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Surface Area (TSA) = CSA + 2 × π × r²

⇒ TSA = 3520 + 2 × (22/7) × 7 × 7

⇒ TSA = 3520 + 2 × 22 × 7

⇒ TSA = 3520 + 308

⇒ TSA = 3828 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 3828 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cylinder

The capacity of the cylinder is given by the formula V = πr²h, where r is the radius and h is the height.

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

CSA refers to the area of the side surface only, calculated as CSA = 2πrh.

Total Surface Area (TSA)

TSA includes both the curved surface and the areas of the two circular bases: TSA = 2πr(h + r).

Base Area of a Cylinder

Each base of a cylinder is a circle with an area of πr².</p

questions.question: The curved surface area of a right circular cylinder is 90.2 m², and its radius is 70 cm, find its height (in m). Take π = (22)/(7)
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

Curved surface area of a right circular cylinder = 90.2 m²

Radius of the cylinder = 70 cm = 0.7 m

π = 22/7

**Concept used: **

Formula for the curved surface area of a cylinder is 2πrh

**Solution:**

Using the formula 2πrh = 90.2 m², we can solve for h.

Substituting the given values, we get 2 × (22/7) × 0.7 × h = 90.2

Solving for h, h = 90.2 / (2 × (22/7) × 0.7) = 20.5 m

**Therefore, the height of the cylinder is 20.5 m.**

questions.question: If 66 cm³ of silver is drawn into a wire having a diameter of 2 mm, then the length of the wire, in m, will be: (Use π = 22/7)

r = radius

questions.question: A cylindrical rod of iron, whose height is equal to the radius of its base, is melted and cast into spherical balls, each of whose radius is half the radius of the base of the rod. Find the number of spherical balls thus made.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **radius** of the **cylindrical rod** be r. Then **height** h = r.

**Radius** of each **spherical ball** = r/2.

Number of balls = Volume of Cylinder ÷ Volume of 1 Sphere

Number of balls = (π × r² × r) ÷ (4/3 × π × (r/2)³) = r³ ÷ (4/3 × r³/8) = 1 ÷ (1/6) = 6.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 balls.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

For **Cylindrical Rod**: Radius = R, Height (H) = R.

For **Spherical Ball**: Radius (r) = R/2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6ea5cc8c49621e1db2e17b128e0f21b017c4f21c68aabe776d040c86f4758fda.png] 

**Formula used:**

**Volume of Cylinder** = πR²H

**Volume of Sphere** = (4/3)πr³

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of **Iron Rod** = π × R² × R = πR³

⇒ Volume of one **Spherical Ball** = (4/3) × π × (R/2)³

⇒ Volume of one **Spherical Ball** = (4/3) × π × (R³/8) = πR³/6

⇒ Number of balls (n) = Volume of Rod ÷ Volume of Ball

⇒ n = πR³ ÷ (πR³/6)

⇒ n = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6 balls.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume Conservation

When a 3D solid is **melted** and recast into new shapes, the **total volume** remains constant.

Cylinder Properties

Curved Surface Area = 2πrh; Total Surface Area = 2πr(r + h).

Sphere Properties

Surface Area = 4πr². For a **hemisphere**, Volume = (2/3)πr³ and Total Surface Area = 3πr².</p

questions.question: Find the number of solid spheres, each of diameter 6 cm, that can be made by melting a solid metal cylinder of height 12 cm and diameter 6 cm.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the **radius (r)** is the same for both the cylinder and the spheres (3 cm), let **n** be the number of spheres.

Volume of Cylinder = n × Volume of Sphere

πr²h = n × (4/3)πr³ ⇒ h = n × (4/3)r

12 = n × (4/3) × 3 ⇒ 12 = 4n

n = 12 ÷ 4 = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

For the **Cylinder**: Diameter = 6 cm ⇒ Radius (R) = 3 cm, Height (H) = 12 cm.

For the **Sphere**: Diameter = 6 cm ⇒ Radius (r) = 3 cm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fd0e86917bb910c76d51c1ee1d379d9a4ec582d2f199c9802175d23f9c04d13b.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Cylinder = π × R² × H

Volume of Sphere = (4/3) × π × r³

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of Cylinder = π × 3² × 12

⇒ Volume of Cylinder = 108π cm³

⇒ Volume of one Sphere = (4/3) × π × 3³

⇒ Volume of one Sphere = (4/3) × 27 × π = 36π cm³

⇒ Number of Spheres = Total Volume of Cylinder ÷ Volume of one Sphere

⇒ Number of Spheres = 108π ÷ 36π

⇒ Number of Spheres = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume Invariance

When one solid object is melted and recast into another shape, the **total volume** remains constant, provided there is no wastage.

Mensuration Formulas

Volume of Cone = (1/3)πr²h and Surface Area of Sphere = 4πr².

Ratio of Volumes

If two solids have the same dimensions (like radius and height), the ratio of the volume of a **Cylinder : Sphere : Cone** is 3 : 2 : 1 (where h = 2r for the cylinder and cone).</p

questions.question: What is the change in the curved surface area of a cylinder when we double the radius and the height is halved?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **Curved Surface Area (CSA)** of a **cylinder** is directly proportional to the product of its **radius (r)** and **height (h)**.

Relationship: CSA ∝ r × h

When the **radius** is doubled (r → 2r) and the **height** is halved (h → h/2):

New CSA factor = 2 (for radius) × 1/2 (for height) = 1.

Since the factor is 1, the area remains the same.

**∴ The correct answer is No change.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Radius = r

Initial Height = h

New Radius (r₁) = 2r

New Height (h₁) = h/2

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a cylinder = 2 × π × r × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e70084523961044f99bf9c4bb6b54e690bdf04030c30085aed6fecc7d5d8f3f2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Curved Surface Area (CSAᵢₙᵢₜᵢₐₗ) = 2 × π × r × h

⇒ New Curved Surface Area (CSAₙₑw) = 2 × π × r₁ × h₁

⇒ Substituting the new values: CSAₙₑw = 2 × π × (2r) × (h/2)

⇒ Simplifying the expression: CSAₙₑw = 2 × π × r × h

⇒ Comparing both: CSAᵢₙᵢₜᵢₐₗ = CSAₙₑw

⇒ Change = CSAₙₑw − CSAᵢₙᵢₜᵢₐₗ = 0

**∴ The correct answer is No change.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cylinder

The volume is given by V = πr²h. If the **radius** is doubled and **height** is halved, the volume becomes 2 times the original volume.

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The TSA of a cylinder is the sum of the curved surface and the two circular bases: TSA = 2πr(r + h).

Area of Base

The area of the circular base is given by A = πr². Doubling the radius results in a 4-fold increase in the base area.</p

questions.question: The ratio of the volume of two cylinders is 27 ∶ 25 and the ratio of their heights is 3 ∶ 4. If the area of the base of the second cylinder is 3850 cm², then what will be the radius of the first cylinder?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **(radius)²** = (V₁/V₂) × (h₂/h₁)

(r₁/r₂)² = (27/25) × (4/3) = 36/25 ⇒ r₁/r₂ = 6/5

Base Area of second cylinder = 3850 ⇒ πr₂² = 3850 ⇒ r₂ = 35 cm

Radius of first cylinder (r₁) = (6/5) × 35 = 42 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 42 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of **Volumes** (V₁ : V₂) = 27 : 25

Ratio of **Heights** (h₁ : h₂) = 3 : 4

**Base Area** of second cylinder = 3850 cm²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8f042bb46114eb942fd73d80798564e1b1e833db735215f45427ff5c753ea728.png] 

**Formula:** Volume of Cylinder (V) = πr²h | Base Area = πr²

⇒ Base Area of second cylinder = πr₂² = 3850

⇒ (22/7) × r₂² = 3850

⇒ r₂² = (3850 × 7) / 22 = 175 × 7 = 1225

⇒ r₂ = √1225 = 35 cm

⇒ V₁ / V₂ = (r₁² × h₁) / (r₂² × h₂)

⇒ 27 / 25 = (r₁² / 35²) × (3 / 4)

⇒ r₁² = (27 / 25) × (4 / 3) × 1225

⇒ r₁² = (9 / 25) × 4 × 1225 = 9 × 4 × 49 = 1764

⇒ r₁ = √1764 = 42 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 42 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cylinder

questions.question: If the curved surface area of a solid cylinder is two-fifths of its total surface area, then what is the ratio of its diameter to its height?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Curved Surface Area (CSA)** to **Total Surface Area (TSA)** is 2 : 5.

In a cylinder, CSA / TSA = h / (r + h).

⇒ h / (r + h) = 2 / 5

⇒ If **height (h)** = 2 units, then **radius (r)** = 5 − 2 = 3 units.

⇒ **Diameter (d)** = 2 × r = 2 × 3 = 6 units.

⇒ Ratio of **Diameter** to **Height** = 6 : 2 = 3 : 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 1.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2/5 × Total Surface Area (TSA)

**Formula Used:**

⇒ CSA of cylinder = 2πrh

⇒ TSA of cylinder = 2πr(r + h)

⇒ Diameter (d) = 2r

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/97bf67c146341cd924da3f24fe3e9fd311df97d8decefbb12080af7903cee0a5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2πrh = (2/5) × 2πr(r + h)

⇒ h = (2/5) × (r + h)

⇒ 5h = 2(r + h)

⇒ 5h = 2r + 2h

⇒ 5h − 2h = 2r

⇒ 3h = 2r

Since **Diameter (d)** = 2r:

⇒ 3h = d

⇒ d / h = 3 / 1

⇒ d : h = 3 : 1

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 1.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cylinder

The amount of space occupied by the cylinder is given by V = πr²h.

Base Area of a Cylinder

The area of each circular face of the cylinder is A = πr².

Surface Area Relationship

The **Total Surface Area** is the sum of the **Curved Surface Area** and the areas of the two circular bases: TSA = CSA + 2 × Base Area.</p

questions.question: The curved surface area of a cylindrical pillar is 528 m² and its volume is 1848 m³ . The ratio between its radius and height is ________.

__Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of **Volume (V)** to **Curved Surface Area (CSA)** of a cylinder is given by **r/2**.

r/2 = Volume ÷ CSA = 1848 ÷ 528 = 3.5

⇒ **Radius (r)** = 3.5 × 2 = 7 m

Using CSA = 2πrh ⇒ 2 × (22/7) × 7 × h = 528 ⇒ 44 × h = 528 ⇒ **Height (h)** = 12 m

Ratio of Radius to Height = 7 : 12

**∴ The correct answer is 7 : 12.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Curved Surface Area (CSA)** of the pillar = 528 m²

**Volume (V)** of the pillar = 1848 m³

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area of cylinder = 2πrh

Volume of cylinder = πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e730a24932b0a26d590cab1c3a1c2c822b0334b4d87f7a3577e412758023e0c1.png] 

Divide Volume by CSA:

⇒ (πr²h) ÷ (2πrh) = 1848 ÷ 528

⇒ r / 2 = 3.5

⇒ **Radius (r)** = 7 m

Now, substitute r in the CSA formula:

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × 7 × h = 528

⇒ 44 × h = 528

⇒ **Height (h)** = 528 ÷ 44 = 12 m

Ratio of Radius (r) to Height (h):

⇒ r : h = 7 : 12

**∴ The correct answer is 7 : 12.**

**__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a Cylinder

The total surface area includes the curved surface and the two circular ends: TSA = 2πr(r + h).

Volume of a Cone

For a cone with the same radius and height as a cylinder, its volume is one-third of the cylinder: V = (1/3)πr²h.

Relationship between r, h, V and CSA

The radius can always be found directly if Volume and CSA are known using the formula r = 2V/CSA.</p

questions.question: If the curved surface area of a solid right circular cylinder of height h and radius r is one-third of its total surface area, then:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of CSA to TSA for a right circular cylinder is CSA / TSA = h / (h + r).

Given CSA is one-third of TSA, so CSA / TSA = 1 / 3.

Equating the ratios: h / (h + r) = 1 / 3

⇒ 3h = h + r

⇒ 2h = r ⇒ h = (1/2)r

**∴ The correct answer is h = (1/2)r.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/04ea252f9d04475afc2898a69f7011af0cf89a407f09da4fe97c631cf9411147.png] 

**Given:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = (1/3) × Total Surface Area (TSA)

**Formula Used:**

CSA of cylinder = 2πrh

TSA of cylinder = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2πrh = (1/3) × 2πr(h + r)

⇒ 2πrh ÷ 2πr(h + r) = 1/3

⇒ h / (h + r) = 1/3

⇒ 3 × h = 1 × (h + r)

⇒ 3h = h + r

⇒ 2h = r

⇒ h = (1/2)r

**∴ The correct answer is h = (1/2)r.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of Cylinder

The volume of a cylinder is given by the formula V = πr²h, where r is the radius and h is the height.

Surface Area of Cone

The curved surface area of a cone is πrl and the total surface area is πr(l + r), where l is the slant height.

Surface Area of Sphere

The total surface area of a sphere is 4πr², as it does not have flat surfaces, its CSA and TSA are the same.

questions.question: The curved surface area of a cylinder, whose height is 10 cm, is 1320 cm². What is the volume of this cylinder? [Use π = frac{{22}}{7}]

**Radius (r)** = **CSA** ÷ (2 × π × h) = 1320 ÷ (2 × 22/7 × 10) = 21 cm.

**Volume (V)** = (**CSA** × r) ÷ 2 = (1320 × 21) ÷ 2 = 13860 cm³.

In m³: 13860 ÷ 10,00,000 = 0.01386 m³.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.01386 m³.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Height (h)** = 10 cm, **Curved Surface Area (CSA)** = 1320 cm², π = 22/7.

**Formula Used:** **CSA** = 2πrh; **Volume (V)** = πr²h.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/70eeacbf4652248c7454cd1478c6832830547c25adcc8e9d409e5e6ef5406c53.png] 

Find the **Radius (r)** first:

⇒ 1320 = 2 × (22/7) × r × 10

⇒ 1320 = (440/7) × r

⇒ r = (1320 × 7) ÷ 440

⇒ r = 3 × 7 = 21 cm

Now, calculate the **Volume (V)**:

⇒ V = πr²h

⇒ V = (22/7) × 21 × 21 × 10

⇒ V = 22 × 3 × 21 × 10

⇒ V = 13860 cm³

Convert **Volume** to cubic meters (m³):

⇒ 1 m = 100 cm ⇒ 1 m³ = 10,00,000 cm³

⇒ V = 13860 ÷ 10,00,000 m³

⇒ V = 0.01386 m³

**∴ The correct answer is 0.01386 m³.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume and Surface Area of Cylinder

For a cylinder of radius r and height h, the Volume is πr²h, the Curved Surface Area is 2πrh, and the Total Surface Area is 2πr(r + h).

Unit Conversion for Volume

To convert cm³ to m³, divide the value by 10⁶ (1,000,000) because (100 cm)³ = 1 m³.

Relation between Volume and CSA

The volume of a cylinder can also be expressed in terms of its curved surface area as Volume = (CSA × r) ÷ 2.</p

questions.question: The curved surface area of a cylindrical pillar is 176 m² and its volume is 352 m³. Find the ratio of its radius to its height.{(Use } pi = (22)/(7) {)}
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Volume (V)** to **Curved Surface Area (CSA)**: V ÷ CSA = (πr²h) ÷ (2πrh) = r ÷ 2.

352 ÷ 176 = r ÷ 2 ⇒ 2 = r ÷ 2 ⇒ **radius (r)** = 4 m.

Substitute r in CSA: 2 × (22/7) × 4 × h = 176 ⇒ (176/7) × h = 176 ⇒ **height (h)** = 7 m.

**Ratio** of radius to height = 4 : 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 4:7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Curved Surface Area (CSA)** of the pillar = 176 m²

**Volume (V)** of the pillar = 352 m³

Value of π = 22/7

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8d7315848f76ec08d71c346dbb7670c63e03619d91d22095a9f57db20a58df13.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πrh

Volume (V) = πr²h

**Calculations:**

⇒ Dividing Volume by CSA: V ÷ CSA = (πr²h) ÷ (2πrh)

⇒ 352 ÷ 176 = r ÷ 2

⇒ 2 = r ÷ 2

⇒ **radius (r)** = 2 × 2 = 4 m

⇒ Now, using CSA formula: 2 × (22/7) × 4 × h = 176

⇒ (176/7) × h = 176

⇒ **height (h)** = 176 × (7/176) = 7 m

⇒ **Ratio** of radius to height (r : h) = 4 : 7

**∴ The correct answer is 4:7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of a Cylinder

It is the sum of the curved surface area and the areas of the two circular bases: TSA = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r).

Volume of a Cone

The volume of a cone with the same radius and height as a cylinder is exactly one-third of the cylinder's volume: V = (1/3)πr²h.

Relation between V and CSA

For any cylinder, the ratio of its Volume to its Curved Surface Area is always r ÷ 2.</p

questions.question: The volume of a metallic cylindrical pipe is 1232 cm³. If its external radius is 7 cm and thickness is 2 cm, then the length of the pipe (correct to one decimal place) ( in cm) is: (Take pi =(22)/(7))
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Inner radius (r)** = **External radius (R)** − **Thickness** = 7 − 2 = 5 cm.

Volume of hollow cylinder = π × (R² − r²) × h

1232 = (22/7) × (7² − 5²) × h ⇒ 1232 = (22/7) × 24 × h

h = (1232 × 7) ÷ (22 × 24) = 8624 ÷ 528 ≈ 16.33 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 16.3 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Volume (V)** = 1232 cm³

**External radius (R)** = 7 cm

**Thickness (t)** = 2 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of **hollow cylindrical pipe** = π(R² − r²)h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b711afbf504c2bb03e6c3b8014159e3f03ca4dcabf777ed5afb269d05ccd90ff.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Inner radius (r)** = R − thickness = 7 − 2 = 5 cm

⇒ 1232 = (22/7) × (7² − 5²) × h

⇒ 1232 = (22/7) × (49 − 25) × h

⇒ 1232 = (22/7) × 24 × h

⇒ h = (1232 × 7) ÷ (22 × 24)

⇒ h = 8624 ÷ 528

⇒ h = 16.333... cm

**∴ The correct answer is 16.3 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Hollow Cylinder Surface Area

Total Surface Area = 2π(R + r)(h + R − r). It includes inner CSA, outer CSA, and the area of two rings.

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

External CSA = 2πRh and Internal CSA = 2πrh.

Volume Calculation

The volume of material in a hollow pipe is the difference between the volumes of the outer and inner cylinders: V = πh(R² − r²).</p
